title: Finite-time clock simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean alphabet, and finite state set $S$, and let $P:S\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a state predicate. There exist a finite-state machine $H$ with $k+1$ work tapes, an injective map $\iota:S\to Q$, and maps $F,U:\mathrm{Option}(S)\to Q$ such that the following holds. For every Boolean input $x$, every initial configuration $c$ of $M$ whose state is $q$, every Boolean word $w$, and every clock-tape offset $a\in\mathbb Z$, suppose the extra tape content $C$ satisfies $C(a+p)$ equals the content of the word $w$ at position $p$ for each integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$. Set $d$ to the natural number represented by the base-two digits of $w$. If, at some time $\tau\le d$, the run of $M$ from $c$ is halted or its state satisfies $P$, and every earlier configuration in that run is neither halted nor in a state satisfying $P$, then for some $T\le 5\tau+2|w|+2$, machine $H$, started from the configuration encoding $c$ with state $\iota(q)$ and extra tape $C$ at offset $a$, reaches the configuration of $M$ at time $\tau$ with state $F$ applied to that configuration's state; before time $T$, its state is never in the image of $F$ or $U$. If no configuration of $M$ at any time $u\le d$ is halted or has a state satisfying $P$, then for some $T\le 5d+2|w|+2$, the same run of $H$ reaches the configuration of $M$ at time $d$ with state $U$ applied to that configuration's state; before time $T$, its state is never in the image of $F$ or $U$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has $k$ work tapes and Boolean alphabet
$P$ is a Boolean predicate on states
For all integers $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, $C(a+p)$ equals the word's content at position $p$
In the finish case, a halted or $P$-marked configuration occurs at time $\tau\le d$
In the finish case, no earlier configuration is halted or $P$-marked
In the timeout case, no configuration through time $d$ is halted or $P$-marked
